title: Definition
text: $$cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$$ is the x-coordinate of the point on the circle that lies along the circumference corresponding to the angle measure $$\frac{5\pi}{6}$$.\n##figure1.gif##

title: $$30-60-90$$ triangle
text: The absolute values of the coordinates of this angle are given by the legs of a triangle with angles of $$30$$, $$60$$, and $$90$$. The hypotenuse has length $$1$$. The y-coordinate length is $$\frac{1}{2}$$. The x-coordinate is obtained from the Pythagorean theorem: $$\sqrt{1^2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$.\n##figure2.gif##

title: Coordinate
text: The point on the unit circle with angle $$\frac{5\pi}{6}$$ is in the second quadrant. Thus, the x-coordinate is negative, so it is $$\frac{\left(-\sqrt{3}\right)}{2}$$.\n##figure3.gif##
